inferred: A defensive deflection can be authored as a brief causal contact that redirects an incoming threat and then splits THREAT_CLOCK from BODY_CLOCK.
The body can continue paying torsion/support debt after contact while the redirected threat travels independently.
Support loss, catch, countertorque, and guard rebind are authored direction choices, not source choreography.

novelty.thesis: Defense is not finished when contact ends: a redirected threat can continue on an independent clock while the body still owes recoil, support, and guard-rebind debt.
novelty.material_difference: one brief shunt contact changes downstream threat trajectory; threat and body then evolve as independent clocks, support debt occurs only after release, and recovery finishes displaced rather than resetting.
